scope: California outer-coast browse sectors (catalog/coastal-sectors.json), north to south. Bays and offshore islands need their own packages and are not inventoried here.

labels.MEASURED: copied or summed from pixel/cell counts already recorded in a repo catalog for exactly the quantity named
labels.ESTIMATED: derived with a stated assumption (sector assignment by bounding box, 0-100 m band standing in for 0-300 ft, reach-level rather than grid-level footprints)
labels.UNKNOWN: no catalog figure exists in the repo; not filled by guessing

tiers.5 m: > 2 m and <= 5 m (also NOAA VR BAG refinements, recorded only as 1-4 m)
tiers.none: no grid with confirmed 0-300 ft cells

definitions.best_tier: finest tier among grids with CONFIRMED shallow cells in the sector: CSUMB nominal_0_300ft_pixels > 0, NOAA BAG 25-200 ft eligible cells > 0, or a seafloor-ledger reach with a selected native footprint in the 0-100 m band. No minimum area. Grids whose depth band is not recorded (most opened USGS DS781 rasters) do not set the tier; they are listed as finer_grids_depth_unrecorded.
definitions.tier_uncertain: true when the tier rests on NOAA VR BAG cells whose spacing is recorded only as 1-4 m, so the true class may be 2 m
definitions.coverage_pct_at_best_tier: ESTIMATED reach-level range from the seafloor ledger (low = reaches using only grids at the tier or finer; high = reaches using any such grid) over the provisional BlueTopo 0-100 m band of reaches wholly inside the sector; UNKNOWN elsewhere
definitions.release_date: publication/release date of the grid; acquisition_dates is a separate field

limits: Grid spacing is not sounding accuracy; no source here is qualified as an MLLW fishing depth.

No repo catalog records a 0-300 ft reference area outside the seafloor ledger (Pigeon Point to Point Conception), and the ledger band is 0-100 m (about 0-328 ft), so every coverage share is ESTIMATED or UNKNOWN, never MEASURED.
The seafloor ledger records one selected native footprint per reach, not per grid, so coverage at a given resolution is a low-high range.
NOAA counts come from bounded audits (files <= 100 MB); larger or failed files are open items, not zeros.
Extent figures are per evidence family and are never summed across families; overlapping surveys within a family are not deduplicated.
This inventory changes no map layer, target, score or export.
